name: Regulatory capacity

subjectOf.text: Mandatory risk disclosure to the SEC would probably fail on staffing grounds, because professionals capable of understanding hedge fund risk data would be disincentivized to use that knowledge for supervision rather than economic gain, finding the private sector far more lucrative.
subjectOf.abstract: Professionals who could understand the risk data would probably be disincentivized to use their knowledge for purposes of supervision rather than economic gain. Knowledgeable risk analysts may find the private sector much more lucrative than the public sector.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: where the regulator must interpret data on hard-to-value assets and complex instruments

subjectOf.text: Neither national nor international regulators have the resources to fully investigate or regulate hedge fund activity, and the industry actively lobbies to preserve the resulting information asymmetries.
subjectOf.abstract: National and international regulators do not have the resources to fully investigate or regulate the activities of hedge funds. Hedge funds are lobbying to preserve information asymmetries as far as possible and avoid enhanced transparency.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Indirect Regulation of Hedge Funds (2019). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3405660

subjectOf.text: The gap between regulators' technical understanding and the state of the art in AI drives rules to one of two failure states: too vague to be enforceable, or so prescriptive that they suppress creative and beneficial uses of AI.
subjectOf.abstract: There is often a gap between the regulators' technical understanding and the state of the art in AI technology. This gap can lead to regulations that are either too vague to be enforceable or overly prescriptive, stifling creative and beneficial uses of AI.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4796714
scope_conditions: applies where regulators lack current technical expertise
